## Context resolved from project knowledge

- **Defect mechanically confirmed by reading the code, not inferred.**
  `--exclude-issue` is declared `type=int` (`scripts/step9c_baseline.py:4441-4447`),
  and `_fleet_gate_issues` drops only `keys.discard(str(exclude_issue))`
  (`:4025-4026`), while the refresh alternate `step9c_baseline\.py refresh` in
  `FLEET_GATE_SIGNATURE_RE` is group-less and therefore maps to the reserved
  literal `FLEET_REFRESH_KEY = "refresh"` (`:3979-3981`, consumed at `:4024`). No
  integer can ever equal `"refresh"`, so the pseudo-issue is unexcludable by
  construction. `_cmd_probe_fleet` then exits 3 at
  `len(grouped) >= _fleet_max()` (default 2, `:4041-4049`).

- **The refresh kick site is one hop from where the body points it.** The body's
  Files of record says `.claude/skills/issue/SKILL.md` Step 9c; since the #2155
  step split the kick actually lives at
  `.claude/skills/issue/steps/13-step-9.md:3826-3840` — detached
  `setsid nohup timeout --kill-after=60s 4650s`, fired when the compare JSON
  reports `stale: true`, with the spec's own instruction "do NOT block this
  verdict on it". The ~77 min contention window is that 4650 s bound.

- **The canonical arbitration is FAIL-OPEN at 2700 s, so the incident's
  "3600 s ceiling then FATAL 90" is not the spec's shape.** The canonical
  paragraph (`steps/13-step-9.md:3220-3247`) queues on a bounded until-loop with
  `[ $SECONDS -gt 2700 ]` and then LAUNCHES ANYWAY, printing
  `[gate-fleet] cap-expired`. No `FATAL 90` / `exit 90` token exists anywhere in
  the main-tree workflow surface (`scripts/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/rules/`
  all clean), so the #2654 first relaunch chain was an ad-hoc composition that
  dropped the fail-open launch-anyway arm. The root defect stands either way — the
  canonical shape would still have burned the full 2700 s — but the "one full hour
  lost" figure is amplified by that chain-composition deviation, which is a
  separate concern from this task's Goal. Logged here rather than filed
  separately (this session carries the workflow-fix posture; the tag is `wf-fix`).

- **A semantics change is fleet-wide: five hooked gate sites consume the one
  canonical paragraph.** 9c 1b / 1c / 1d, both Step 10d gate blocks, and the
  Step 9a-ter inline payload lint gate — call sites at
  `steps/13-step-9.md:1258, 3227, 3235, 3630` and
  `steps/18-step-10d.md:1056, 3781`.

- **Sibling task #2563 is a DISTINCT defect in the same probe family, not a
  duplicate.** It covers the per-issue `probe --issue N` form counting a sibling
  WATCHER (a Monitor whose own cmdline carries the gate pattern) as a live gate;
  different probe form, different mechanism, different remedy. It shares the
  design space "which exclusion classes does the probe honor" and the same file,
  so the planner should coordinate rather than merge. It sits at `proposed` with
  no live session, so there is no concurrent-writer collision today.

- **Test home is unambiguous.** `tests/test_step9c_baseline.py` is the only file
  referencing `_fleet_gate_issues` / `FLEET_REFRESH_KEY` / `EPM_GATE_FLEET_MAX` /
  `exclude_issue`. Spec-recipe-text sync tests that may pin the arbitration
  paragraph if it is edited: `tests/test_issue_skill_gate_single_flight.py`,
  `tests/test_issue_skill_gate_recipe_hardening.py`,
  `tests/test_issue_skill_lint_family_sync.py`.

- **Lineage.** #1962 (completed, 'daily-fix: cross-issue lint-gate concurrency
  arbitration') introduced `probe --fleet` and the cap; #2256 recomposed the
  signature union to the script-file forms. Parent #2654 carries the 30/30
  contender census and the FATAL-90 chain record.
